messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed for redwood-hosted-us-east-azd on ELB (target group tg-rtv-1122). Automated severity: P1. Traffic spike + route oscillation detected. Please acknowledge with /ack.
Maya: acked. seeing sustained 502/504s from ELB across several AZs in azd, ~12% error rate. users reporting timeouts to inference endpoints.
Tony: copying graphs now. CPU/NET on instances look fine, but ELB health checks are flapping healthy->unhealthy for a subset of targets. Could be kernel-level RSTs or network path issue.
Ashley: @Maya do we have any recent deploys? I see none in last 30m. Tagging infra team.
Oncall-SRE: I’m on pager. pulling ELB logs -> filtering 502/504 via nginx backend. Early hint: connections reset mid-stream with TCP reset from host.
Maya: also seeing increased Route53 weighted failover churn, some clients briefly go to eu-west fallback. Not full failover but oscillation. Could be DNS TTL interaction + ELB target oscillation.
Tony: running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...` shows ~20% targets Unhealthy in azd-1c only. Other AZs healthy.
Maya: starting emergency mitigation: 1) set Route53 weight for us-east-azd -> reduce by 50% to relieve pressure 2) set ELB deregistration delay to 10s 3) scale up healthy pool in other AZs.
DevOps-Bot: Chef run queued: scale group redwood-serve-us-east-azb +3 instances. ETA ~4m.
Oncall-SRE: manual change to Route53 weighted record done: reduced weight for azd from 60 -> 20, propagated (console change id r53chg-7643). Expect ~30-45s for clients honoring TTL.
Ashley: starting graceful drain of suspected hosts (i-0a1b2c3d) - marking Unhealthy and triggering replacement.
Tony: Capture of kernel logs from i-0a1b2c3d shows many `TCP: time wait` + `nf_conntrack` table nearing limit. Could be conntrack exhaustion causing resets.
Maya: increasing conntrack size on node pool via sysctl on the hot hosts as immediate mitigation: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`
Oncall-SRE: also adjusted iptables conntrack timeouts to be slightly lower to recover slots quicker.
ProductOps: any confirmed customer impact? We have several API error spike alerts. Notifying SRE leaders and CS.
Maya: impact summary for comms: ~12% error rate for /generate endpoints in us-east for ~20 minutes, affecting ~8% of requests globally due to weighted DNS oscillation. Key customers may see errors or increased latency while retrying.
Tony: rolling replacement in azd will continue. If replacements fail, plan B is to fail traffic away from azd entirely via Route53 (set weight 0) and announce maintenance.
DevOps-Bot: ASG scaled +3 healthy instances registered. ELB target counts stabilizing in azb/azc.
Oncall-SRE: ELB Unhealthy count in azd down from 20% -> 4% after conntrack bump and drains. 5xx rate dropped to ~2%. Monitoring for 10m window.
Maya: Good. Keeping P1 open until stable 5xx <1% for 30m. Please document all actions.
Tony: note for postmortem: investigate kernel conntrack defaults, NAT gateway conntrack saturation, and health-check cadence vs TTL interactions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity P1 -> Monitoring. Pager rotation: Maya hands to Tony at 3498130800. Use incident channel for communications. Incident timeline snapshots stored at https://internal.redwood/incident/3498129930
ProductOps: drafting customer comms: "We experienced elevated errors due to an AZ-level networking condition impacting ELB target health in us-east-azd; traffic was shifted to healthy AZs and the issue mitigated. We will follow up with root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:
Maya: handing off to Tony. Thanks everyone."
